plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This holds because your payment depends only on others' bids, not your own bid, so shading up or down only risks losing profitable wins or winning at a loss. With a value of $26, the optimal action is to bid exactly $26, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay less than my value when I do win.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy: if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning at a price above your value (loss); if you bid lower, you risk losing an item you'd have profited from. This holds regardless of the other bidders' strategies, since the payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (unless you're the winner). Therefore, I will bid exactly my value, $18, to guarantee optimal expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bid wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do—there's no incentive to shade up or down, since your payment depends on others' bids, not your own bid amount (as long as you win). Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $21.
